definitions.explanation: A longer, indirect route taken instead of the most direct path, whether by necessity (road closure) or by choice.

definitions.gloss: roundabout approach; indirect way of doing something
definitions.explanation: A figurative detour — taking a longer or less efficient approach to achieving a goal. Can imply either inefficiency or a valuable learning experience.

examples.japanese: ⟦{工事|こうじ}{中|ちゅう}→工事中：09625_koujichuu⟧な⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で{回|まわ}り{道|みち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: There was construction, so I took a detour.

⟦{急|いそ}いでいる→急ぐ：01191_isogu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{回|まわ}り{道|みち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦させられて→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{困|こま}った→困る：00861_komaru⟧。
examples.english: I was in a hurry and was frustrated at being forced to take a detour.

notes:
USAGE:
{回|まわ}り{道|みち} can be used as a noun or as a suru-verb ({回|まわ}り{道|みち}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ — to take a detour). The figurative sense is very common, especially when reflecting on life choices or career paths.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {回|まわ}り{道|みち}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (take a detour)
- {回|まわ}り{道|みち}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (turn out to be a detour)
- ⟦{人生|じんせい}→人生：03355_jinsei⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{回|まわ}り{道|みち} (life's detours)
- ⟦{少|すこ}し→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧{回|まわ}り{道|みち}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (take a slight detour)

SIMILAR WORDS:
⟦{迂回|うかい}→迂回：09034_ukai⟧ means "detour" in a more formal or technical sense, often used for traffic or military contexts. ⟦{遠回|とおまわ}り→遠回り：14380_toomawari⟧ means "going the long way around" and is close in meaning but emphasizes distance.
